title: Biotech news from around the world - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A news roundup noting India's $9 million state investment in Bengaluru AI drug-discovery firm Peptris Technologies under the VIGOR program, and China's 2026-2030 pharma five-year plan targeting 25% of all first-in-class drugs plus 50 domestic drugmakers above $1.5 billion in annual sales.

themes.theme: State-funded AI drug discovery in India

insights.claim: Bengaluru-based Peptris Technologies received a $9 million investment from India's Department of Science and Technology under the government's VIGOR program to accelerate AI-based drug discovery.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: India is directly funding AI-pharma platforms; state capital is becoming a competitive input in the AI drug-discovery race.

insights.claim: The Peptris project is scoped to advance four experimental drugs to technology readiness levels, covering preclinical development, validation and preparation for clinical trials.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Milestone-based public funding tied to named assets gives a measurable timeline against which to judge AI-discovery claims.
insights.locator: The project aims to advance four experimental drugs

insights.claim: China's latest five-year plan for its pharmaceutical industry sets development of at least 25% of all first-in-class drugs as one of ten objectives.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: An explicit innovation-share target signals sustained policy support for Chinese novel-drug developers and more competition for Western pharma pipelines.

insights.claim: From 2026 to 2030 Chinese policy will back drugmakers pursuing new targets, mechanisms and modalities, focused on major infectious and chronic diseases plus rare and pediatric conditions.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Flags the therapeutic areas where Chinese-originated assets are most likely to emerge for licensing over the next five years.

insights.claim: China's plan also targets 50 domestic drugmakers with at least $1.5 billion in annual sales and five globally blockbuster products.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Scale targets of this kind imply consolidation and export ambition among Chinese pharma; a watch item for global market share.
insights.quote: Other objectives include 50 domestic drugmakers having at least $1.5 billion in annual sales and five products being blockbusters globally.
